correctness.rationale: In finite dimensions the approximate definition is equivalent by compactness to the existence, for each admissible functional, of a norming vector \(y\) with both \(f(y)=1\) and \(\|x+y\|_\infty=2\). For \(f=(a_i)\in S_{\ell_1^n}\), every nonzero coefficient forces a norming vector coordinate \(y_i=\operatorname{sgn}(a_i)\). If \(x\in\{-1,0,1\}^n\setminus\{0\}\), either a saturated coordinate has zero functional coefficient and can be chosen freely, or \(f(x)\ge0\) forces some saturated coordinate whose sign agrees with its coefficient, yielding norm two. Conversely, if \(0<|x_j|<1\), placing small total opposite-sign mass on all saturated coordinates and the remaining mass with the sign of \(x_j\) gives \(f(x)>0\) while every norming vector cancels every saturated coordinate, so \(\|x+y\|_\infty<2\). This proves exactly the nonzero ternary coordinate locus and the cube-face-center count \(3^n-1\).
residual_risks: The argument is finite-dimensional and does not extend automatically to the full dual of infinite-dimensional \(\ell_\infty\).
